{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the bottom line of the fish, stroke 2. It forms the belly and the underside of the body, so it is a large part of what makes the outline read as a fish. I traced it from the nose and laid about 25 dominoes across several batches, then stood back up the few that were knocked over. The finished run falls from the start through nearly all of the standing dominoes.

Execution: I picked up the bottom line as soon as the top line reached the nose and worked on it steadily. After I laid the first stretch, I inspected the belly several times to find where the chain was weak. I stood dominoes back up where needed, so the belly stayed connected through to the push. When the time got tight, I handed the tail end to a teammate so the line could be finished from both directions. I stayed clear of the others' hands at the end so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I told the table early that I had the bottom line and kept them updated on where my line stopped. I agreed the handoff point for the tail end, so we avoided working within a few units of each other. I stepped back once the tail was being built, and I kept the table informed through to the final hands-off call.

Leadership: I took a defined piece of work, committed to it out loud, and delivered it. I made the handoff decision on the bottom line myself and then moved to checking joins. That kept the table's critical path moving and helped us finish with time to spare.", "my_share_percent": 28}
